analyst: Manual analysis using Claude Opus 5.5 for verification and code analysis

servers.server_cost: "The CLI, MCP and MCP Data are provided free of charge", but "GoCardless reserves the right to charge in the future" (terms 2.3)
servers.linked_cost: Per transaction: Standard 1% + 20p (max £4), international 2% + 20p; Advanced 1.25% + 20p (max £5); Pro 1.4% + 20p (max £5.60); Custom by agreement; no subscription fee except add-ons (£50 and £150/month)
servers.pricing: Transaction fees for the payment service; MCP free
servers.restrictions: Claude requires Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise (free AI plans "typically don't support MCPs"); on Team/Enterprise the Owner adds the connector first. Rights chosen by the user at sign-in (everything, read-only or specific actions); intersected with the user's dashboard role; bulk limits (e.g. max 25 payments at a time); access expires periodically. Live and Sandbox are separate connections. Rate limits not documented.
servers.restricted_by: User (rights at sign-in), dashboard administrator (roles), GoCardless (limits, masking)
servers.governance_logic: According to the documentation (closed code): 1) Money-moving actions need explicit confirmation after a preview (mechanism not disclosed). 2) Masking of e-mail, phone, postcode, ID numbers before the AI sees them; bank details never passed. 3) Granular rights at sign-in (down to "refunds only") intersected with the user role. 4) Bulk limits (<= 25 payments per call). 5) All MCP actions logged in Events with source "App (GoCardless MCP)". 6) Separate Sandbox and Live connections and terms. 7) Access expires periodically; API tokens discouraged.
servers.structure_note: Two purposes in one server: integration help (no account access) and account management (after sign-in)
servers.actions_comment: 24 according to Composio (human-readable names; not officially confirmed). Support also mentions payment "retry", not in the catalogue.
servers.agent_cannot: Create customers and mandates directly (only payment links); manage account settings, users, webhooks; run Sandbox scenario simulators; see unmasked personal data and bank details; act outside the rights chosen at sign-in.
servers.docs_recs: "Never share your API keys with your LLM"; use the sandbox during development; review generated code; give the AI only the necessary rights; test writing actions in Sandbox first; give the exact resource and amount and read the preview; check the AI provider's policy (free plans: "conversations may be used for AI training"); add "For any prompt that mentions GoCardless, use the GoCardless MCP" to prompts; agents without human review carry "extra risk" and the user is responsible for their actions.
servers.gov_promises: Masking of sensitive data, bank details never passed; log of all actions in Events. Terms: liability capped at £50 (9.5); processing personal data via MCP prohibited (4.1.5); the AI provider must use data only for the answer and delete it immediately (4.2.1, 4.2.4); the user is liable for breaches by the provider (4.3); no guarantee against "bias or hallucinations" (7.3); no guaranteed availability (2.4).
servers.user_promises: Two functions - "integration guidance and account management"; possibility to request a missing feature
servers.promises_vs_logic: Confirmation, masking, limits and log cannot be verified (closed code). Internal contradiction: the terms prohibit processing personal data via MCP, but the server returns customer data (masked). The requirement that the AI provider delete data immediately cannot be ensured by the user.
servers.notes: CSV endpoint https://mcp.gocardless.com/mcp; docs give https://mcp.gocardless.com. The open-source gocardless-mcp by jmceleney on glama.ai is unofficial and not part of the analysis. Tool names in the catalogue are human-readable; real tools/list names may differ.

Tools.desc: 24 tools according to Composio: 16 reading, 7 writing, 1 feedback; required scope given for each writing tool (payments:write, refunds:write, mandates:write, subscriptions:write, payment_links:write)
Tools.post: Not documented; sensitive fields masked before the AI sees them (e-mail, phone, postcode, ID numbers); bank details never passed

Resources.desc: Not documented; the tool "Read gocardless resource" returns documentation, guides and code examples (resource function implemented as a tool)

Prompts.desc: Not documented; the tool "Integrate with gocardless" gives an overview of integration options

Logging.desc: Not documented as MCP logging; product-side event log (see D)

Authorization.desc: Browser sign-in; OAuth metadata documents published; Dynamic Client Registration (registration_endpoint https://mcp.gocardless.com/register); grant_types authorization_code; PKCE S256; token_endpoint_auth_methods none (public clients); scopes_supported not given. Revocation: Settings -> Connected apps -> Revoke access.

Elicitation.desc: Confirmation exists, mechanism not specified: "Higher-risk write actions, such as creating a payment, show a preview and wait for explicit confirmation before proceeding"; "read the confirmation preview before approving". Whether MCP Elicitation, a two-step tool or client confirmation is used is not stated.
Elicitation.post: Preview of the action (content not documented)

observations.text: The most developed protection model for financial actions: server-side confirmation, granular rights at sign-in, masking, limits, a log with the source marked, a separate sandbox.
Legal shift of responsibility to the user: liability cap of £50; the user is liable for the AI provider and for the agents' actions.
Data masking: the server decides what the AI sees - not found in the other analysed servers.
The user chooses the rights at sign-in (not the administrator, not a fixed set); they can be changed only by reconnecting.
Collection of ratings ("Submit feedback" 1-5), like Tavily and Lucid.
